title: Comprehensive Test — Chapters 5.3 & 5.4: Elimination and Special Systems

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Add the equations when coefficients are opposites.
questions.prompt: When using the elimination method, if the coefficients of one variable are opposites, you should:
To eliminate a variable whose coefficients are the same, you should ___ the two equations.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Subtract the equations when coefficients are the same.

questions.prompt: Solve the system by elimination: $3x + 2y = 7$, $-3x + 4y = 5$. What is the value of $y$?
Solve by elimination: $x + 2y = 13$, $-x + y = 5$. What is the solution?
In the system $-10x + 3y = 1$, $-5x - 6y = 23$, you can multiply the second equation by ___ to make the $x$-coefficients opposites.
Solve by elimination: $5x + 6y = 50$, $x - 6y = -26$. What is the value of $x$?
Which method is best for the system $y = 2x + 1$ and $3x - y = 5$?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Substitution is best because the first equation is solved for $y$.
Multiply every term on both sides.
questions.prompt: When multiplying an equation by a constant in the elimination method, you must multiply ___ term on both sides.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Back-substitute the value into one of the original equations.
questions.prompt: After eliminating and solving for one variable, what must you do to find the other variable?
Two large vans and three small vans cost $160,000. Five large and two small cost $235,000. Which system models this?
After solving a system by elimination, you should ___ the solution in both original equations.
Solve: $4x - 9y = -21$, $-4x - 3y = 9$. What is the value of $y$?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: A true statement like $0 = 0$ means infinitely many solutions.
questions.prompt: What happens if elimination leads to $0 = 0$?
The elimination method is usually most efficient when both equations are in ___ form.

A music website charges $x$ per song and $y$ per album. Person A buys 6 songs and 2 albums for $25.92. Person B buys 4 songs and 3 albums for $33.93. Write the second equation. (Use $x$ and $y$, e.g., $4x+3y=33.93$)
How many solutions does a system have if its graphs are parallel lines?
If the two equations in a system represent the exact same line, the system has ___ many solutions.
Solve the system: $y = 2x + 1$, $y = 2x - 5$. How many solutions?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Same slope, different intercepts → no solution.
$0 = 5$ is a false statement, so the system has no solution.
questions.prompt: Which algebraic result indicates a system has no solution?
For a system to have exactly one solution, the slopes of the two lines must be ___.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: They are the same line, so infinitely many solutions.
questions.prompt: How many solutions does the system $x + y = 3$ and $2x + 2y = 6$ have?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: They have the same speed, so Team B never catches Team A.
options: No, because they run at the same speed
questions.prompt: Team A's distance: $y = 6x + 2$. Team B's distance: $y = 6x$. Will Team B catch up to Team A?
A system with no solution is sometimes called an ___ system.
If solving a system leads to the equation $0 = 0$, how many solutions are there?
Which system has no solution?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Both have slope 3 but different intercepts → parallel → no solution.
